story.title: The Borrowed Pulse
story.logline: A man who rents out his extra heartbeats to desperate people discovers his own clock has already stopped.
story.twist: He has been dead for three days, surviving only on the belief that he is still trading time.
story.ending: Who is currently beating inside your chest?

scenes.narration: My heart beats twice as fast because I sold half my life to save a drowning stranger.
scenes.visual_prompt: Close-up of Leo, a 25-year-old man with messy dark hair and a faded gray hoodie, pressing his hand to his racing chest in a dimly lit, narrow alley.
scenes.camera: Extreme close-up tracking shot, shaky vertical framing

scenes.narration: The broker said I had thousands of hours to spare. He paid me cash for every single missing thump.
scenes.visual_prompt: Leo, 25, dark hair, gray hoodie, standing inside a cramped, neon-lit pawnshop counting a thick stack of hundred-dollar bills with trembling fingers.
scenes.camera: Medium eye-level shot, sharp focus on hands

scenes.narration: At first, I felt invincible. I bought the car, the apartment, all the things I never thought I could afford.
scenes.visual_prompt: Leo, 25, dark hair, gray hoodie, sitting in a sleek, modern, empty apartment, laughing brightly while tossing car keys in the air.

scenes.narration: Then the fatigue crept in. My chest felt hollow, like an empty drum echoing in a vast, cold room.
scenes.visual_prompt: Leo, 25, dark hair, gray hoodie, slumping heavily against a cold concrete wall inside his luxury apartment, clutching his chest in pain.

scenes.narration: I called the broker to buy my time back, to reverse the trade before my engine completely ran out.
scenes.visual_prompt: Leo, 25, dark hair, gray hoodie, frantically pressing numbers on a cracked smartphone inside his dark living room, sweat dripping down his pale face.

scenes.narration: The line was dead. The neon shop downtown was completely gone, replaced by a brick wall covered in dust.
scenes.visual_prompt: Leo, 25, dark hair, gray hoodie, staring blankly at an old, abandoned brick storefront covered in thick spiderwebs and peeling paint.

scenes.narration: A passerby walked right through me, dropping his coffee as a sudden, freezing chill filled the empty street.
scenes.visual_prompt: Leo, 25, dark hair, gray hoodie, standing motionless on a rainy sidewalk while a startled pedestrian phases through him, spilling coffee.
scenes.camera: Static wide shot with depth of field

scenes.narration: I looked down at my hands and saw they were translucent, glowing faintly like fading embers in the dark.
scenes.visual_prompt: Leo, 25, dark hair, gray hoodie, raising his glowing, semi-transparent hands to the streetlamp light, eyes wide with absolute terror.
scenes.camera: Macro hand focus shifting to face

scenes.narration: I didn't sell half my life. I sold all of it three days ago in that alleyway accident.
scenes.visual_prompt: Flashback glimpse of Leo, 25, dark hair, gray hoodie, lying still and lifeless on wet asphalt next to a crashed motorcycle under flashing police lights.

scenes.narration: If I am already dead and gone... who is currently beating inside your chest right now?
scenes.visual_prompt: Leo, 25, dark hair, gray hoodie, staring directly forward through the phone screen into the viewer's eyes with a haunting, knowing smile.

caption.hook: His heart beat on borrowed time.
caption.title: The Borrowed Pulse
caption.caption: He spent his life renting out extra heartbeats to those desperate to cheat death. But when he finally checks his own chest, he realizes his clock stopped three days ago—and he's only surviving on pure denial. Would you keep walking if you knew you were already gone?
